cases.titulo: When an E2E test breaks, who is to blame?
cases.problema: QA teams spend hours deciding whether a failing test is flaky, the environment is down, there is a real bug, or the test is outdated. I saw this firsthand while monitoring critical user journeys at Voidr.
cases.abordagem: I built an agent that gathers evidence from Playwright traces, classifies the cause with a model trained on labeled cases, and uses a local LLM to write the report and suggest a new selector. GitHub Actions deliberately injects failures every 3 hours, so the correct diagnosis is always known.
cases.resultado: 98.4% accuracy across 192 failures, compared with 77.1% for manual rules; 20 out of 20 on previously unseen cases. The first model caught 0% of real bugs; three clues a person would use fixed that.

cases.problema: At Shippify, I worked on routing for clients such as Amazon, Mercado Livre and Natura. I wanted to understand the problem beyond the company's code, using open data.
cases.abordagem: A pipeline using SPTrans GTFS and live GPS data (22,274 stops, 1,349 routes), a hexagonal map of transit access, and a capacity-constrained route planner that runs in the browser.
cases.resultado: 11–29% fewer kilometers than nearest-neighbor dispatch, using the same fleet. I also showed that the official timetable does not predict where buses slow down (R² of −0.10), which is why the speed model uses GPS data.

cases.problema: Genomic data is hard to explore for people who do not code. I experienced this during my undergraduate technology research at INTERAGRO, working with over 200,000 bovine genomic records.
cases.abordagem: A Python pipeline that retrieves genes from Ensembl, finds Cas9 cut sites, and checks for off-target matches against an index of 5.9 million sites in the human exome, presented through four browser games.
cases.resultado: 25 genes, 8,107 cut sites, and a test requiring identical scores from the Python and TypeScript implementations for every published guide RNA.
